details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cna.title: Xen Orchestra: Empty-object login token

descriptions.description: CWE-1287: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input

descriptions.value: XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and perform unauthorized actions within the context of the application. This is MTLVULN-1877.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an arbitrary file upload attack due to insufficient file type validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

cna.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability

descriptions.value:
A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software.

This vulnerability is due to the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled on a device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by selecting the UEFI Shell boot option at boot time and using available shell commands to modify UEFI memory variables. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to manipulate the preboot environment, overwrite UEFI Secure Boot-related memory values, and execute unauthorized software on the affected device.

exploits.value:
The Cisco PSIRT is aware that proof-of-concept exploit code is available for the vulnerability described in this advisory.

The Cisco PSIRT is not aware of any malicious use of the vulnerability that is described in this advisory.

Authenticated Accounts Users can send crafted requests naming payment documents of other companies, outside their User Permissions, or already submitted, to alter clearance dates and compromise bank reconciliation integrity.

Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.

Authenticated clients can advertise a small max_datagram_frame_size and trigger a UDP response, causing a slice bounds panic that crashes the server.

cna.title: web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10 Missing Authentication in Chacha20Poly1305 Key Encryption

descriptions.value: web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10, jwt-experimental before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a missing integrity check in the experimental Chacha20Poly1305 key-encryption algorithm, which discards the Poly1305 tag in encryptKey() and calls openssl_decrypt() without it in decryptKey(). Attackers on the token path can modify the encrypted content encryption key undetected.

cna.title: diaspora* through 0.10.1 SSRF via GET /link Endpoint

descriptions.value: diaspora* through 0.10.1, using the diaspora_federation gem through 1.2.0, contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the pod send requests to arbitrary internal hosts by supplying a crafted diaspora handle to the GET /link endpoint, which triggers WebFinger discovery without private-address filtering. Attackers can specify a handle containing an IPv4/IPv6 address and port such as diaspora://probe@host:port to force the HttpClient to connect to loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or cloud metadata addresses, enabling blind probing of the pod's internal network.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: diaspora* through 0.10.1 Unauthenticated SSRF via WebFinger Discovery in /link Endpoint

descriptions.value: In authd before 0.7.2, an improper access control vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to complete a first-time SSH login with another account's UID and incorrect primary GID, and to read or modify files owned by that account.
